addr-extern.desc: data reached through an address-suffixed extern instead of fixing the split/owner

cast-addr-alias.desc: a local seen through another type via a pointer cast of its address

data-object-reshape.desc: Data object boundaries changed against retail symbols.txt (one retail object split into several globals, or several retail objects merged into one array) to steer codegen or relocs.
data-object-reshape.example: Example: retail `sVlcDefaultPtrs` (size 0xB0) split into `sVlcDefaultPtrs`..`sVlcDefaultPtrs_5`, while other code still indexes `sVlcDefaultPtrs + 0x28` past the new bound.

decl-drift.desc: A local/import declaration retyped so it disagrees with the callee's actual definition (extern "C" hides the mismatch at link time).
decl-drift.example: Example: `extern "C" u32 bdatResolveItem(u32, u16, u32);` in CtrlObjectParam.hpp while CfBdat.cpp defines `bdatResolveItem(u32 owner, u32 itemId, u32 flags)`.

reorder-vs-original.desc: reordering statements/members against a known original to change register or schedule
reorder-vs-original.why: semantic: depends on the original's order

scalar-self-view.desc: re-reading one member through a local pointer to it

sdk-idiom-rewrite.desc: rewriting a known SDK/middleware idiom (BTE macro, nw4r, CRI, MSL, RVL SDK) to steer codegen
sdk-idiom-rewrite.example: expanding a BTE macro by hand

single-use-inline.desc: new file-local static inline helper with one call site, added to steer codegen
single-use-inline.example: static inline f32 getX(const S* s) { return s->x; }

steer-temp.desc: A named scalar temporary introduced (or reused, or applied to only some of several parallel expressions) solely to sequence stores or move register allocation.
steer-temp.example: Example: `s32 v = 0; *out1 = v; v = 1; *out2 = v;` instead of `*out1 = 0; *out2 = 1;`; or splitting only the R channel of an R/G/B triple into conv/prod temps with swapped operands.
